page.overview:
What is Asaari Wind?

The Asaari Wind was a SoroSuub Personal Luxury Yacht 3000 owned by the Bimm crime lord Ritinki around 0 ABY. The vessel was heavily modified by the Bimm, and featured luxurious appointments and offensive capabilities far in excess of its original specifications.

During a summit held by Ritinki and the Rodian kingpin Vop on the Ithorian Herdship Song of the Clouds, the Asaari Wind was commandeered by the thief Cecil Noone and his partners-in-crime, with Ritinki being killed in the course of the theft. Under Noone's ownership, the yacht operated under the aliases Hieroglyph, Spiraling Shape, Tailchaser, and Voona's Dream II. The vessel sustained severe damage amid the crew's frantic escape from the planet Kabal after Noone's dealings with the Krish business magnate Tyro Viveca went awry.

The Asaari Wind was a Personal Luxury Yacht 3000 manufactured by the SoroSuub Corporation. While in the ownership of the Bimm crime lord Ritinki, the Asaari Wind had been modified. Its armaments included two light laser cannons and two medium ion cannons, all of which were linked and front-mounted and could be fired from the bridge, and twin heavy laser cannon turrets, as well as a rear-facing turbolaser mounted in place of the external observation platform typical of most yachts.

The Asaari Wind could reach sublight speeds of 1,000 kilometers per hour, and was equipped with shields and sensors, as well as primary and secondary hyperdrives. The latter, and the yacht's standard repulsorlifts and ion engines, were replaced with components used in much larger ships, including state-of-the-art Sienar Fleet Systems drives. A slave circuit paired with a beckoncall transmitter enabled Ritinki to summon the Asaari Wind remotely; having been designed exclusively for Ritinki by a moonlighting Industrial Automaton engineer, the transmitter activated the yacht's engines and used the ignition command as a homing signal, which guided the ship to the Bimm's location. Measuring fifty meters in length, the Asaari Wind could carry seventy metric tons of cargo, and accomodated two crewmembers and three gunners for basic operations, with a skeleton complement of between one and ten. The yacht also had capacity for ten passengers, and toted a month's worth of consumables.
